newsitem.title: CANADA: Caisse to vote against Avenor-Repap merger.
newsitem.headline: Caisse to vote against Avenor-Repap merger.

text.p: The Caisse de depot et placement, Quebec's public pension fund manager, said on Monday it planned to vote against the proposed merger of Avenor Inc and and Repap Enterprises Inc.

After a media conference, Caisse officials told reporters that discussions with other institutional holders of Avenor indicated that most of them would also vote against the proposed merger under the current terms of the C$2.75 billion deal.

Asked if the Caisse would vote against the merger, first vice-president Michel Nadeau said, "Yes", adding that the Caisse had great reservations about the size of the debt load the proposed merged entity would carry.
"We have spoken to others (institutions) and most of them express reservations," Nadeau said.
Jean-Claude Scraire, chairman and chief executive of the Caisse, said the pension fund manager urged Avenor to consider other "avenues or options" to the Avenor-Repap merger as it now stood.
Scraire said that the Caisse held just under 10 percent of Avenor's shares, adding that he did not think institutional shareholders held enough shares to block the proposed merger.
Denis Aubin, chief financial officer of Avenor, said he believed the Repap merger would close on schedule.

"Clearly we want to complete the Repap transaction on Wednesday. We believe we have got strong support from our shareholders. We need two-thirds. We believe we're there," Aubin said in a telephone interview.

Domtar Inc approached Avenor last week about starting merger discussions, Avenor said in an earlier statement. Avenor said a senior Domtar executive approached it, indicating that Domtar wanted to pursue negotiations with Avenor "with a view to enter into a pre-merger agreement within 72 hours."
Avenor said it turned away the suitor so it could focus on its soon to close acquisition of Repap.
The Caisse, with C$51 billion of assets under management, is Canada's largest institutional investor.
The pension fund holds 21 percent of Domtar shares, and the Societe generale de financement (SGF), a Quebec government investment agency, holds another 24 percent.
The Quebec government, through these two agencies, effectively controls Domtar.
